correctness.rationale: The affine ring identifies with the two Artin–Schreier equations over k[t,t^-1] by t=B+A, t^-1=B-A; its monic free presentation embeds in the generic fiber. Each nonzero F_p-combination has a simple pole at 0 or infinity, so the generic fiber is a field of degree p². Locally the regular terms are Artin–Schreier coboundaries over k[[u]] and the simple-pole coefficient spans rank one exactly for c=1, rank two otherwise. Nontrivial inertia characters have Swan one, hence the different is 2(e-1). The contributions of the two branch fibers give the stated values by Riemann–Hurwitz and Deuring–Shafarevich. Above infinity the leading terms of x^p and y^p agree, so x/y tends to 1, and above zero they are opposite, so x/y tends to -1. All branches at infinity are thus accounted for. Direct expansion gives distinct tangents and p smooth branches at c=1, and otherwise the unique tangent of multiplicity p-1 with intersection order p and one normalization branch. The two delta invariants in either case agree with the degree-2p arithmetic genus. The affine derivatives rule out further singularities.
residual_risks: The small-field count is a consistency check, not itself evidence for all-prime ordinarity or all coefficients of the zeta numerator; those conclusions of the Finding use the mathematical argument as stated, not an extrapolation. The broader recorded script runs were not independently reproduced.
